base_member_text: [L19-L33,L45-L341] (LOW/global-state API) The library exposes one saved global model state with no initialized/finalized guard, leaving repeated init, calls before init, and calls after final as undocumented lifecycle hazards.
audit_member_text: [L19-L33,L45-L225] (MED/lifecycle) Module state is saved globally and init has no already-initialized guard or cleanup path, so repeated initialization can reinitialize MPI and reallocate persistent model/output state.
[L321-L341] (MED/lifecycle) final has no initialized/finalized guard and always finalizes logging and MPI, making duplicate finalization or finalization before successful init unsafe.

base_member_text: [L228-L239] (MED/undefined/stale status) outputext tests the library module's stale error variable rather than receiving a status from output, and leaves its function result undefined for error values other than 0 or 1.
audit_member_text: [L228-L237] (HIGH/uninitialized-result) outputext assigns its function result only when module error is exactly 0 or 1, leaving the C-visible return value undefined for any other error code.

adversarial.rationale: Ordinary timesteps set error to 0 or 1, so this is not a general post-step failure. However, MPI decomposition warnings 5/6 survive init (xmpi.F90:404-406; logging.F90:274-279), and a direct outputext call before the first executestep can encounter them and leave its result undefined.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L278-L316] (HIGH/error propagation) executestep suppresses a nonzero timestep error by skipping physics but then unconditionally increments the step count and returns success.
audit_member_text: [L278-L316] (HIGH/error-propagation) executestep sets error through timestep and skips physics on failure, but then unconditionally increments the completed-step count and returns success zero.

adversarial.rationale: timestep can set ierr=1 on its defuse path (timestep.F90:727-760), after which executestep skips physics but still increments n and assigns result 0. outputext subsequently consults the shared error flag, but direct executestep clients receive the wrong success status and completed-step count.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex independent skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L75-L115,L153-L225] (MED/initialization status) init passes a shared error variable through setup operations but never checks or propagates it and unconditionally returns success after output initialization.

audit_member_text: [L267-L287] (LOW/argument-contract) The optional custom timestep has neither intent nor value semantics, leaving its mutation and language-binding contract unclear to callers.
[L287-L291] (MED/error-side-effect) Output schedules and progress logging are advanced immediately after timestep reports an error, before the error guard that suppresses the physical update.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The ordering exists, but timestep.F90:L747-L759 deliberately forces final diagnostic output and moves scheduled times to the failure time before setting ierr=1. Updating output counters before skipping physics serves that error-output path; advancing diagnostic logging is not evidence of the claimed erroneous side effect.

audit_member_text: [L269-L274,L330-L336] (MED/uninitialized-timing) MPI finalization passes saved t01 to timing output even though t01 is assigned only when execute_counter equals 1, so short or failed runs can finalize with an undefined loop-start timestamp.
dispositions.rationale: span-confirmed: t01 has no initializer and is first set on the second executestep call because execute_counter starts at zero. A one-step MPI run reaches final and passes t01 to writelog_finalize, which subtracts it without a step-count guard.
